prerequisites: Knowledge of symbols, specific graphics, electrical diagrams

learning_outcomes.text: Proper implementation of specific fundamental knowledge of mathematics, physics, chemistry, in the field of electrical engineering
Use of fundamental concepts of computer science and information technology
Use of fundamental knowledge of electrotechnics
Design of electrical systems and their components
Design and coordination of experiments and tests
Diagnosis, troubleshooting and maintenance of electrical systems and components
Identification of the objectives to be achieved, available resources, conditions to complete them, working stages, working times, associated deadlines and risks
Identification of the roles and responsibilities in a multidisciplinary team and use of relationship and effective working techniques in the team

Effective use of information and communication sources and assisted professional training (Internet portals, specialized software applications, databases, online courses etc.) both in Romanian and in a foreign language.
Acquire basic knowledge regarding reliability indicators of elements and systems and main phenomena occurring in the operation of electrical appliances.
Acquire knowledge regarding the maintenance of electrical equipment.
Develop skills and competencies in the issue of correct choice of equipment that is part of electrical installations.
Acquire practical skills in electrical maintenance, construction, research, operation, repair and maintenance of electrical, electromechanical, electrothermal installations.

Study the quality of electrical equipment and devices, identify electrical supply diagrams of electrical equipment, and familiarize with modern means of measuring temperature and electrical parameters during the operation of electrical equipment.
Understand the complexity, usefulness and maintenance of these facilities and treat them as such.
Form skills to address the specific problems faced by a specialist in the field of electrical engineering.

syllabus_topics: History of the development of reliability, diagnoses and qualities, notions, composition and representations. High-performance systems. Efficient systems
Reliability indicators of elements and systems. General reliability indicators of irreparable elements
Modeling the defects of the electrotechnical devices
Structural redundancy of elements and systems. Modeling the failure of the elements. Modeling of wear processes. Modeling fatigue processes
Indicators and methods for evaluating the reliability of electrical equipment. General aspects regarding the reliability of electrical equipment
Systematic analysis of the forecast reliability of electrical equipment. Predictive reliability analysis of power transformers
Estimation with confidence intervals. Accuracy estimation with confidence intervals. Design of reliability tests
Case study on the operational reliability of electrical equipment. Methodological considerations on the study of operational reliability. Global indicators of operational reliability of subsystems
Behavior of systems with renewal in finite time intervals. Availability. Types of renewal
Optimum problems in the field of electrical equipment maintenance. Optimization criteria for maintenance problems. Optimizing the allocation of human potential for the execution of maintenance works
Reliability allocation engineering. Reliability prediction and allocation. Maintenance allocation prediction. Reliability testing
Modern technologies for the maintenance of electrical equipment. Technical diagnosis of electrical equipment

Global modeling of systems reliability through Markov processes. Markovian modeling of systems. Modeling Markov processes for the global description of a system without renewal. Modeling Markov processes for the global description of a system with renewal
Structural modeling of systems reliability by Markov processes. Markov process model for a serial system. Markov process model for a parallel system
Labor protection standards specific to electrical equipment. Basic notions and concerns in reliability

Laws of distribution of random variables. Distribution functions and probability function. Characteristic sizes. Distributions of discrete and continuous random variables. Probabilistic functions in the reliability of the simple element
Evaluation of reliability indicators based on equivalent reliability diagrams. Solving some proposed applications
Determining the reliability indicators of systems with active reserve elements using Markov chains with continuous parameter
Evaluation of the reliability indicators of the systems with elements in reserve applying the method of Markov chains with continuous parameter
Testing of vibration electrical equipment
Preventive and corrective maintenance of switching devices
Vibration test of electrical contacts
Shock test of electrical equipment
Applications of reliability in technology
Teaching seminars and holding them
teaching_methods: Teaching subjects and involving students in dialogues
Requesting student contributions on course-specific topics
Presenting notions related to labor protection specific to electrical equipment by the teacher
Test regarding theoretical knowledge related to the seminar
assessment_rules: The final grade (N) is calculated as N = 0.75Ex + 0.25LF, where Ex is the exam grade and LF is the seminar grade. To pass, the student must achieve a minimum grade of 5 for the exam, 5 for the seminar, and 5 for the report/synthesis material (R), meaning N>=5, LF>=5, R>=5. The exam consists of 3 topics from the course, each requiring at least a grade of 5 to pass the exam. All seminar papers must be performed to be eligible for the exam, and only one remaining seminar can be recovered in the last week of the semester.
